page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g5ne.2xlarge is a general-purpose virtual server instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 4 physical Intel Xeon 8163 processor cores running at 2.5 GHz. The instance is configured with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying instead on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 4 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations indicate that the ecs.g5ne.2xlarge delivers modest compute capabilities. In stress-ng and Geekbench testing, both single-core and multi-core CPU performance fall into the bottom 25% tier. Memory bandwidth tests show a weak read-only performance of 327.1 GB/sec for small cached blocks and 38.97 GB/sec for large uncached blocks, though large block write bandwidth reaches average levels at 34.64 GB/sec. Cryptographic and integer operations are supported via AVX, AVX512F, AES, and BMI2 instruction sets, yielding an average Passmark CPU score of 6968.94.

The primary tradeoff of this instance is its lower processing efficiency compared to newer hardware generations, as evidenced by poor single-threaded gzip compression and low LLM inference speeds on 7B models. However, the dedicated CPU allocation and balanced memory-to-vCPU ratio offer stable, predictable performance for workloads that do not require high-speed local storage or intensive computational throughput. It is qualitatively cost-effective for legacy enterprise applications, moderate web serving, and basic database operations that fit within its 4 Gbps network baseline.

Operating on the KVM hypervisor, this instance provides a balanced 4.0 GB of memory per core but lacks local storage and GPU accelerators. Performance benchmarks place its compute and memory capabilities largely in the lower 25% tier, with a Passmark CPU score of 6968.94 and a baseline network bandwidth of 4 Gbps. While single-core processing and memory read bandwidth are weak, the instance maintains average large-block write speeds and stable dedicated resource allocation. It is best suited for moderate, non-compute-intensive workloads such as basic web serving, lightweight database operations, and general-purpose enterprise applications.
